surprises.head: The Rangers couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: The Rangers usually get some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 4.5% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.8% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Stecher wins it with 28 seconds left
paras: Easton Cowan opened the scoring for the Maple Leafs less than two minutes in, but Mika Zibanejad tied it 1-1 for the Rangers just over four minutes later. Teddy Blueger scored his first goal for Toronto less than five minutes later to put the Maple Leafs back ahead 2-1. The second period was a wild one. Oliver Bjorkstrand and Tye Kartye scored just under four minutes apart early in the period to turn a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 lead. Brandon Duhaime scored his first goal for Toronto a minute and a half later to tie it 3-3. Kirill Marchenko put the Maple Leafs up 4-3 on the power play late in the second. Alexis Lafrenière tied it 4-4 for the Rangers with less than six minutes left, but that was the last goal the Rangers would get. Troy Stecher put the Maple Leafs ahead for good with 28 seconds left. Duhaime finished with a goal and two assists, and the Rangers’ Adam Fox had four assists.

The Maple Leafs drove the play, outshooting the Rangers 35-25, and the scoreboard caught up. The Rangers hit two posts and came up a goal short. Sergei Bobrovsky made 21 saves for the Maple Leafs, and Dylan Garand allowed five goals on 35 shots. The Leafs moved to 6-4-2 and climbed to fourth in the Atlantic, while the Rangers fell to 7-4-1, second in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Adam Fox passed James Patrick for tenth on the Rangers’ all-time assists list, with 364.
Three straight wins for the Maple Leafs.
The Rangers have gone winless in four straight on the road.
Troy Stecher scored his first goal of the season, his first since Feb 2 (32 games played since).
